artworks.title: Phrixus and Helle
artworks.description: This plate after a Pompeian fresco shows Phrixus and Helle on the golden ram — the children of Athamas and the cloud-nymph Nephele, fleeing Ino's plot. Nephele's gift of Hermes' ram is the hinge of the Golden Fleece cycle even when she herself stays off-stage.

artworks.title: Phrixus and Helle crossing the Dardanelles
artworks.description: A Stabiae mosaic from the Villa of San Marco freezes Nephele's children mid-flight: the golden ram she sent bears Phrixus and Helle toward Colchis until Helle falls and names the Hellespont. Roman floor art remembers the cloud-mother's rescue as the Fleece's origin.

artworks.title: Helle on a Ram
artworks.description: This Metropolitan Museum relief isolates Helle on the golden ram — Nephele's daughter mid-passage, the cloud-mother's gift made visible as a single rider. The Fleece story begins with Nephele's rescue long before Jason sails.

popCulture.title: Golden Fleece
popCulture.description: Nephele's ram, sent to save Phrixus and Helle, yields the fleece Jason later seeks — the cloud-nymph as the mythic source of the Argonaut prize.

popCulture.title: Nephele
popCulture.description: Cloud-wife of Athamas, mother of Phrixus and Helle — the nymph whose rescue of her children against Ino opens the Colchian fleece saga.

popCulture.title: Hellespont
popCulture.description: The strait still bears Helle's name — Nephele's daughter who fell from the ram her mother sent, geography remembering the cloud-nymph's children.
